title: ML-MT122-MtDispatchComposer

scope.summary:
GOAL: Build the MT dispatch composer — the Handshake component that turns a governance microtask contract (an hsk.microtask_contract@1 JSON file, the EXACT shape used in .GOV/task_packets/*/MT-NNN.json — verified against .GOV/templates/MICRO_TASK_CONTRACT_TEMPLATE.json and the real example WP-KERNEL-012/MT-045.json) into a governed worker launch. This productizes what the operator's repo-gov orchestrator does by hand today: read the MT contract, inject role + contract into a coder session, launch it in a lane. The product READS the contract file shape; it NEVER writes .GOV.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: One new backend module src/backend/handshake_core/src/swarm_orchestration/mt_dispatch.rs (contract parser + payload composition + lane policy + spawn call + dispatch record), wired into swarm_orchestration/mod.rs, plus tests with FIXTURE contracts under the crate's test tree (never pointing at .GOV).

DETAILED SPEC:
1. Contract ingestion — pub struct MicrotaskContractDoc, parsed from raw JSON (pub fn parse_microtask_contract(raw: &str) -> Result<MicrotaskContractDoc, ContractParseFailure>). Required fields read: schema_id (MUST be "hsk.microtask_contract@1"), wp_id, mt_id, lifecycle.status + lifecycle.depends_on, scope.summary, scope.allowed_paths, scope.forbidden_paths, scope.acceptance_criteria, scope.proof_targets. ALL other fields (gui_obligation, red_team, implementation_notes, validation blocks...) MUST be tolerated and ignored — real contracts carry many extra keys (MT-045 is the reference fixture shape). Typed error pub enum ContractParseFailure: MalformedJson { reason }, UnsupportedSchema { found }, MissingField { path }, NotDispatchable { status } (dispatch refuses contracts whose lifecycle.status is a terminal/validated state; PENDING/OPEN/claimed-for-work states are dispatchable per policy flag).
2. Payload composition — pub fn compose_worker_payload(contract: &MicrotaskContractDoc, role: &RoleRef, policy: &MtDispatchPolicy) -> WorkerLaunchPayload, delegating section assembly to the MT-083 worker prompt composer. The composed payload MUST carry, as distinct sections: (a) role overlay (role_id resolved via the Roles layer; child-role semantics per MT-086); (b) OBJECTIVE = scope.summary verbatim; (c) BOUNDARIES = allowed_paths + forbidden_paths verbatim, framed as hard scope; (d) OUTPUT FORMAT = the hsk.mt_signal@1 JSON Schema from MT-121 mt_signal_json_schema(), declared as the REQUIRED structured exit (transport binding: --json-schema on the Claude lane per MT-027, --output-schema on the Codex lane per MT-046, final-message parse on ACP); (e) PROOF-TARGET EXPECTATIONS = scope.proof_targets verbatim with the instruction that each executed target becomes one evidence[] entry in the exit signal; (f) acceptance_criteria verbatim.
3. Lane choice — pub struct MtDispatchPolicy { lane_selector: LaneSelector, dispatchable_statuses: Vec<String>, ... }; LaneSelector resolves a model lane (local or cloud) per policy (explicit lane pin, else role-default). NO new spawn path: the actual launch goes through SwarmCoordinator::spawn_session (the single sanctioned spawn path — coordinator.rs:548), so caps, consent gates, breaker, and claim leases all still apply.
4. Dispatch record — pub struct MtDispatchRecord { dispatch_id, wp_id, mt_id, session_id, model_lane_id, role_id, payload_sha256, dispatched_at_utc }; returned to the caller AND recorded (event on the swarm event sink + persisted alongside the session per existing session-record conventions) so MT-123 can open the run as DISPATCHED and receipts can correlate.

STEP-BY-STEP:
1. Read coordinator.rs (spawn_session, SessionHandle, lane store), model_lane.rs, and the MT-083 composer surface in the product worktree; match their conventions.
2. Implement parse_microtask_contract + ContractParseFailure with serde against a permissive struct (serde default + flatten-tolerant); add fixture JSONs under the test tree: one full-shape contract copied structurally from the MT-045 example (ids anonymized), one minimal contract, one malformed, one wrong-schema, one terminal-status.
3. Implement compose_worker_payload delegating to MT-083; assert section presence and verbatim boundary/proof-target inclusion by test.
4. Implement dispatch(contract, role, policy) -> MtDispatchRecord calling SwarmCoordinator::spawn_session; in tests use the crate's existing fake/test lane caller pattern (see coordinator tests) — no live CLI required in this MT.
5. Emit the dispatch event; assert via RecordingSwarmSink (events.rs) that dispatch produces exactly one dispatch event carrying wp_id/mt_id/session_id.
6. Run proof targets.
forbidden_paths: app/src/** (legacy React; GUI surface exception exists only on the board MT MT-125)
.GOV/** (the product READS MT contracts; it never writes .GOV — tests use fixtures, not .GOV paths)
acceptance_criteria: parse_microtask_contract ingests the full real-world contract shape (fixture structurally mirroring WP-KERNEL-012 MT-045.json) reading wp_id, mt_id, lifecycle, scope.summary/allowed_paths/forbidden_paths/acceptance_criteria/proof_targets, and tolerates all extra keys.
Wrong schema_id, malformed JSON, missing required field, and terminal lifecycle.status each yield the correct typed ContractParseFailure variant — never a silent default and never a spawned worker.

compose_worker_payload output contains role overlay, verbatim objective (scope.summary), verbatim boundaries (allowed_paths + forbidden_paths), the hsk.mt_signal@1 schema as required output format, and verbatim proof-target expectations — each asserted by test.
dispatch() launches ONLY via SwarmCoordinator::spawn_session; grep-level proof that mt_dispatch.rs contains no process spawn primitive (no Command::new / tokio::process) of its own.
Every dispatch produces an MtDispatchRecord with payload_sha256 and exactly one dispatch event observable on a RecordingSwarmSink.
cargo build -p handshake_core green; new tests green.
expected_tests: full-shape fixture contract parses; extra keys ignored
typed failures: MalformedJson / UnsupportedSchema / MissingField / NotDispatchable
payload sections present + verbatim boundaries/proof targets + mt_signal schema embedded
dispatch via coordinator fake-lane produces MtDispatchRecord + one dispatch event
no self-owned spawn primitive in mt_dispatch.rs
implementation_notes: The governance contract file is the interface, not the storage: Handshake ingests the JSON the orchestrator (or a future in-product taskboard) hands it. Do not build a .GOV directory walker in this MT; the caller supplies raw contract JSON (path reading is the caller's concern and keeps this module .GOV-agnostic and disk-agnostic per GLOBAL-PORTABILITY).

Reuse MT-083's composition API rather than string-formatting a prompt here; this MT only defines WHAT sections the MT-dispatch payload must carry. If MT-083's API lacks a section kind needed here, extend it there via its declared extension seam (coordinate through depends_on, do not fork composition logic).
payload_sha256 exists so a dispatch is reproducible/attributable: same contract + role + policy => same hash; hash the composed payload bytes, not the file path.
Lane choice policy stays minimal here (pin or role-default); richer routing lives in the coordinator's existing routing surface — do not duplicate routing.rs logic.
NotDispatchable statuses default-deny: only statuses explicitly listed in MtDispatchPolicy.dispatchable_statuses (default ["PENDING", "OPEN"]) may spawn.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Headless dispatcher MT; operator-visible dispatch rows ship on the board MT MT-125.

user_manual_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Internal dispatch plumbing; the UserManual entry for the MT dispatch loop lands with MT-126/MT-125.

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.obligation: MtDispatchRecord (ids, lane, role, payload hash, timestamp) is the machine-readable dispatch state a no-context model can query.
One dispatch event per launch on the swarm event sink, correlatable by wp_id/mt_id/session_id.
Deferred to MT-125 (board row per dispatch); recorded here as the consuming surface.

risk_if_missed: No mechanical bridge from governance MT contracts to worker launches — the operator keeps hand-injecting contracts through the ACP bridge and the productized loop (MT-123..126) has no entry point.

risks: RISK-1: A second spawn path sneaks in (dispatcher launching processes directly), bypassing SwarmCoordinator caps, consent gates, and claim leases — privilege-escalation surface.
RISK-2: Boundary sections (allowed/forbidden paths) get summarized or paraphrased during composition, so the worker never sees the hard scope verbatim and edits out-of-scope files.
RISK-3: Dispatching a contract in a terminal/validated lifecycle state silently re-runs completed work or clobbers validation state.
RISK-4: Tests read real .GOV contract files, coupling product tests to governance content and breaking the repo-governance/product split.
RISK-5: Contract text is attacker-controllable input to a prompt; a malicious 'summary' could try to override the role/output-format sections.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): only SwarmCoordinator::spawn_session may spawn; proof target greps mt_dispatch.rs for process primitives and requires zero.
CTRL-2 (RISK-2): tests assert byte-verbatim inclusion of allowed_paths/forbidden_paths/proof_targets in the composed payload.
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): default-deny dispatchable_statuses allowlist + NotDispatchable typed refusal, covered by a negative test.
CTRL-4 (RISK-4): fixtures live in the crate test tree; .GOV/** is a forbidden path for this MT.

CTRL-5 (RISK-5): composition places contract-derived text in clearly delimited data sections AFTER the role/output-format sections (MT-083 section ordering), and the output-format section is always composer-owned, never contract-derived.

research_provenance.source: WP-017 stub research basis (Anthropic multi-agent worker-prompt structure: objective/output-format/boundaries/effort; Claude --json-schema, Codex --output-schema) + verified governance shape: .GOV/templates/MICRO_TASK_CONTRACT_TEMPLATE.json + .GOV/task_packets/WP-KERNEL-012-.../MT-045.json (real-world extra-key density) + verified product code: coordinator.rs spawn_session:548 / SessionHandle / RecordingSwarmSink in events.rs.
corrections: Contract parser must be permissive-read (real contracts carry validation blocks, repair plans, waivers far beyond the template) — strict-read against the template shape would reject production contracts like MT-045.
Dispatcher composes; it does not route — lane selection defers to existing coordinator routing surfaces to avoid duplicating routing.rs.
